adminNewsletter.noLibraries: The media server did not report any libraries.
adminNewsletter.noneSent: No issue has been sent yet.

adminNewsletter.subject: Subject
adminNewsletter.subscriberCount: {count} subscriber(s). People subscribe themselves on their profile page — an admin cannot sign anyone up.
adminNewsletter.subtitle: A recently-added digest for the people who asked for it. Delivery uses the SMTP settings of the email channel under Notifications.
adminNewsletter.timeFrameHint: How far back the issue reaches. Checked on the normal activity poll, so the server has to be running at that hour.
adminNewsletter.uniqueIdHint: The last sent issue stays available at {path} for anyone signed in. Letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens only.
app.name: Watcharr
chart.describe: Chart of {count} values, total {total}, highest {peak} at {value}.
chart.describeStacked: Stacked chart of {series} over {count} buckets, peak {peak}.
clients.subtitle: Which apps and devices people actually use.
clients.title: Client Statistics
clients.uniqueClientsInfo: Different player applications, e.g. the web app or an Android TV client.
clients.uniqueDevicesInfo: Different browsers, phones or TVs reported by the media server.
common.title: Title
config.backupHint: Written to data/backups next to the database, oldest deleted once the count above is exceeded. Same one-time download as before is still on the {link} page.
config.defaultLanguageHint: What everyone sees who has not picked a language on their own profile.
config.digestHint: Watch time, top titles and active streams over the period, sent as a {code} event to every channel subscribed to it — most useful on email.
config.geoipEnabled: Look up the country of remote streams
config.geoipHint: Off by default, because it sends viewer addresses to a third party. Use {ip} as the placeholder. Local streams are never looked up, and results are cached.
config.monitoringHint: Checked on every activity poll. Firing sends the "monitoring threshold exceeded" event above to every subscribed channel, at most once per 15 minutes per rule. Leave a field empty to turn that check off. Recent alerts are listed below.
config.newAddressAlert: Alert on a successful login from an address the account has never used
config.subtitle: Applies to the whole deployment. Server connections live under Servers.
config.title: Settings
config.transcodeAlert: Alert while any stream is transcoding
config.watchedThresholdHint: Percent of the runtime a stream has to reach. Changing it re-labels past sessions too, because the split is computed on read.
config.webhookHint: Receives a raw JSON POST per event. For ntfy, n8n or anything else that accepts arbitrary JSON. Discord, Slack, Telegram, Pushover, Pushbullet and email have their own channel types under {link}, formatted for what each expects. Leave empty to send nothing here.
dashboard.peakInfo: The busiest moment on record in this period, and what those streams were doing.
dashboard.title: Server dashboard
error.notFound.body: This page does not exist, or it belongs to a feature an admin has turned off for this deployment.
error.notFound.title: Nothing here
error.page.body: The page could not be rendered. This is usually the media server being unreachable or slow to answer — the rest of Watcharr keeps working.
error.page.title: Something stopped this page
event.digest: Periodic summary (see Settings for the schedule)
event.mediaAdded: New media appears in a library
graphs.bandwidthNote: Only the remote half costs uplink. The same stream to a TV in the next room and to a phone on mobile data is the same number and a different problem.
graphs.subtitle: Plays come from the media server's history and reach back before Watcharr was installed. Stream and bandwidth figures come from playback sessions, which start on the day it was.
history.subtitle: {count} plays recorded.
ip.noGeo: No geolocation data. Country lookup is off, or the provider returned nothing — see Settings.
item.playsInfo: Every recorded playback of this exact item.
libraries.neverStartedHint: {count} of {total} titles have no play in your history.
libraries.none: The media server did not report any libraries.
libraries.sectionInfo: Opens this library's own usage figures.
libraries.subtitle: What is on the server, what arrived recently, and what is still sitting there unwatched.
libraries.tableSubtitle: Every library on the server, what is in it and how much of it gets watched.
library.allTimeInfo: Plays counted from the media server's own history, so this reaches back before Watcharr was installed.
library.mediaInfoHint: What the media server reports about the files themselves. Blank cells are fields this backend does not report — Plex has no file for a series, only for its episodes.
library.noItems: The media server did not report any items for this library.
library.showingLimited: Showing {shown} of {total}. The CSV export has all of them.
login.differentServer: Sign in to a different server
login.plexFailed: Could not start the Plex sign-in flow
login.plexHint: Approve the request in the Plex window. If it did not open, use this link:
monitor.failedLogins: {count} failed logins from {ip} in the last {minutes} minutes
monitor.newAddress: {username} signed in from a new address: {ip}
newsletterMail.footer: You receive this because you subscribed in Watcharr. Unsubscribe on your profile page.
newsletterMail.nothing: Nothing was added in this period.
newsletterMail.period: The last {days} days on the server.
notifications.logSubtitle: Every attempt, successful or not — a channel that silently stopped working shows up here instead of vanishing after its one retry.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.subtitle: Destinations for playback, server and monitoring events, on top of the generic webhook on {link}.
overview.streakInfo: Consecutive days with at least one play. Opens your year in review.
overview.watchedTotal: You have watched {duration} on this server.
overview.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of everything you played in the last 30 days.
person.titlesInfo: Credits matched against the watch history by title, since no media server reports TMDB ids.
profile.language.label: Language
profile.languageHint: Stored with your account, so it is the same on every device. The deployment default is {default}.
profile.nlOff: The newsletter is currently switched off by the administrator, but you can still subscribe for when it is turned on.
profile.nlSchedule: Sent every {weekday} at {hour}:00, covering the last {days} days.
profile.sessionsSubtitle: Every device currently signed in as you. Signing one out is immediate.
security.subtitle: Recent sign-in attempts, successful and failed.
servers.confirmRemove: Removing "{label}" deletes its accounts and their history in Watcharr. Type the name to confirm:
servers.name: Name
servers.subtitle: Every connected media server. Each account belongs to exactly one of them, and the sign-in screen only offers a choice while more than one is configured.
serverstats.bingeInfo: Most plays of one title by anyone within a single day.
serverstats.completionInfo: Streams that reached {percent}% of the runtime. Recorded sessions only, so it starts from the day Watcharr was installed.
serverstats.distinctTitlesInfo: Different movies and shows watched server-wide.
serverstats.libraryItemsInfo: Movies and series reported by the media server, cached for five minutes.
serverstats.peakConcurrentInfo: The most streams that ever overlapped in this period, and how they were being delivered at that moment.
serverstats.peakHourInfo: Hour of the day with the most playback starts.
serverstats.subtitle: Usage across all users.
serverstats.title: Server Statistics
serverstats.usersWithPlaysInfo: Users that have at least one recorded playback. Opens the user list.
serverstats.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of every play by every user in the period. The arrow compares it with the period before.
setup.intro: Connect your first media server. You can add more servers later.
setup.title: Set up Watcharr
stats.activeDaysInfo: Days in the period with at least one play.
stats.bingeRecordInfo: Most plays of one title within a single day.
stats.busiestDayInfo: The single day with the most watch time in your whole history. Opens that day.
stats.deliverySubtitle: Recorded from your own sessions since {date} — {count} sessions so far.
stats.finishedFrom: Counted as finished from {percent}% of the runtime.
stats.libraryExploredInfo: Share of the movies and series in your libraries that you have started at least once.
stats.longestPlayInfo: Runtime of the longest single thing you watched.
stats.streakInfo: Consecutive days with at least one play, counting back from today.
stats.subtitle: Your viewing habits. Hover anything for the exact number; a title, a genre, a day or an hour opens the plays behind it.
stats.swipeDay: Swipe sideways for the rest of the day.
stats.swipeStrip: Swipe the strip sideways, tap a frame for that day.
stats.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of every play in the period. The arrow compares it with the period before.
stats.whenYouWatchHint: Minutes per weekday and hour, across your whole history. Click a cell to see what was playing in that slot.
streams.empty: No streams recorded for this period.
streams.subtitle: {count} recorded streams. Sessions are kept after playback ends, which is what makes this history possible at all.
suggestions.empty: Watch a few titles first — suggestions need some history to work with.
suggestions.subtitle: Based on the genres, decades and formats you already watch. Refreshed daily.
system.autoSnapshotsOff: Automatic snapshots are off — enable them on Settings.
system.liveSessionsInfo: Sessions currently reported by the media server. Recorded sessions feed the transcoding and client statistics.
system.mediaServersInfo: Every connected media server that answered a status request.
system.restoreNote: Restore by stopping the container and replacing data/watcharr.db — swapping it while the app is running would corrupt the WAL.
system.subtitle: Connection and sync health for this deployment.
terminate.prompt: Stop this stream? Optional message for the viewer:
title.playsInfo: Every recorded playback, including repeats of the same episode.
title.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of all recorded playbacks.
transcoding.directPlayInfo: Share of sessions the server delivered without re-encoding.
transcoding.sessionsInfo: Playback sessions observed by the activity poller.
transcoding.subtitle: How the server delivered content. Recorded from live sessions, so numbers start at zero on a fresh install and grow as people watch.
transcoding.title: Transcoding Statistics
users.confirmDemoteSelf: Give up your own global admin rights?
users.confirmPromote: Make {username} a global admin of every server?
users.distinctTitlesInfo: Different movies and shows, episodes grouped under their show.
users.longestStreakInfo: Longest run of consecutive days with at least one play.
users.noAddresses: No streams recorded yet. Addresses come from playback sessions, which start collecting from the day Watcharr was installed.
users.noStreams: No streams recorded yet. Sessions start collecting from the day Watcharr was installed, unlike the history.
users.sessionsSubtitle: Every device currently signed in as this user. Signing one out is immediate.
users.subtitleGlobal: Everyone known to this deployment. Import pulls in server accounts that never signed in.
users.subtitleServer: Everyone on your server. Import pulls in accounts that never signed in.
users.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of every recorded play.
watchlist.subtitle: Titles you plan to watch. Plex watchlists are synced automatically.
wrapped.genreFan: You are a {genre} fan — {share}% of everything you watched
wrapped.subtitle: Everything you watched, counted.
wrapped.title: Your Year in Review
wrapped.titlesInfo: Different movies and shows, episodes grouped under their show.
wrapped.watchTimeInfo: Sum of the runtime of everything you played this year. Opens the statistics.
wrapped.yearInDaysHint: {count} days with activity. Tap a frame to see what ran that day.
